target_demo: 20s-30s mobile-native urban Korean adults, Toss app users curious about lesser-known in-app services and Seoul public-bike (Ttareungi) users

production_signature.signature_note: Vertical 9:16 creator-style how-to: opens with live-action presenter at a Seoul Ttareungi bike station holding a labeled CONTENT card, hard-cuts to a single continuous in-hand phone screen-recording covering the full Toss app rental flow (전체 tab -> 따릉이 -> map -> 대여하기 -> 이용권 -> 결제 -> 완료), hard-cuts to a live-action macro of the bike lock QR being scanned by the phone, then a backward-tracking payoff of the presenter walking the unlocked Ttareungi down a sunny winter sidewalk, ending on a hand-stamped paper sticker end card 'Curator T / 토스를 발견하다'. Low intentional camera shake; bright natural daylight; clean Toss blue-and-white UI; bottom-center pill-style subtitle captions throughout.

global_layout.layout_note: Live-action shots place subject/phone center; the long middle section is a centered in-hand phone screen recording with the Toss UI filling most of the frame; every section carries a rounded grey translucent pill caption at lower-center; end card is a single small sticker centered on near-white paper with heavy negative space.

inferred_creative_thinking.insight: Most people only know Toss for transfers and banking and have no idea it can rent a Seoul public Ttareungi bike, so the most persuasive ad is simply showing the full real flow end to end so it feels effortless and trustworthy
inferred_creative_thinking.persona: A curious mobile-native city dweller in their twenties or thirties who already keeps the Toss super-app on their home screen and loves discovering hidden time-saving features that consolidate errands into one app
inferred_creative_thinking.moment: Standing next to a public shared bike and realizing you do not need a separate Ttareungi app or T-money card because the app already in your pocket handles selection, payment and unlock in under a minute
inferred_creative_thinking.product_role: Toss positions itself as an all-in-one super-app whose hidden services quietly absorb everyday public-life tasks like renting a city bike, using payment credentials already registered in the app
inferred_creative_thinking.punchline: The bike you walk past every day can be unlocked with the finance app you already trust, no extra app, card or sign-up needed
inferred_creative_thinking.differentiator: A fintech that demonstrates breadth not by talking about money but by walking you through an unexpected public-mobility service hidden inside the same app, paid with the card already on file
inferred_creative_thinking.brand_fit_one_liner: A super-app that earns loyalty by quietly turning out to do one more useful everyday thing than you expected

inferred_brief: Create a vertical 32-second how-to short demonstrating Toss's lesser-known public-bike (Ttareungi) rental service by walking the viewer through the entire in-app flow as a continuous screen recording bookended by live-action of a presenter at a real Seoul bike station, with step-by-step voiceover mirrored by on-screen subtitles, a QR-unlock payoff and a creator signature end card.
analyst_notes: 5 shots from 4 confirmed hard cuts (scenedetect + metrics diff spikes at 4.404 [69.7], 22.289 [95.9], 26.193 [94.4], 29.396 [87.1]). The 4.40-22.29 segment is ONE continuous in-hand phone screen recording: captions and Toss UI screens change (전체 tab -> 따릉이 mode -> map -> 대여하기 -> 이용권 selector -> 결제 -> 1일권 구매 완료) but the live framing (hand holding phone over a Ttareungi front wheel, blurred sunny street bg) never cuts, so it is treated as a single shot per spec. Shot 3 (22.29-26.19) is a continuous live-action macro: the bike's black lock housing with white QR sticker numbered 57322 and a green release lever, with the phone brought in to scan; Toss scanner screen reads 'QR코드는 안장 밑에 있어요 / 문자 코드 입력하기'. Shot 4 (26.19-29.40) is a continuous backward-tracking payoff of the presenter walking the unlocked mint-green Ttareungi (basket reads 따릉이) down a tree-lined winter Seoul sidewalk past the station kiosk. Shot 5 (29.40-31.70) is a hand-stamped paper sticker end card reading 'Curator T' in blue with '토스를 발견하다' beneath it — this is the content creator's signature sign-off (a Toss-discovery series), not an official Toss corporate logo lockup. Whisper text_raw mis-hears 따릉이 as 다른/다른 길 throughout; corrected against on-screen subtitles which mirror the VO. Brand UI (Toss blue, 토스뱅크 체크카드, 토스증권, 토스페이) verified from native-res frames. No wiggle/parallax global effect (mean_abs_shift_x 0.25, low). Logo marks kept generic in image prompts; on-screen Korean caption and UI text preserved verbatim.

Below the housing, a bright grass-green rubber release lever protrudes from the black mechanism, and the dark bike frame tube and a softly blurred spoked wheel and black saddle recede out of focus behind. Across the lower-center of the overall frame sits a rounded translucent grey subtitle pill with white Korean caption text reading exactly '인식하면'. Lighting is bright neutral natural daylight from above around 5600K acting as a medium-hard key at roughly 3:1, throwing defined small shadows from the hardware and glinting off the black plastic, with the phone screen adding cool self-emission. The colour palette is dominated by near-black lock plastic (#1C1C1C), clean white of the QR sticker and phone UI (#FFFFFF), a punchy public-bike green (#3DBE4A) on the lever, neutral grey pavement (#B7B7B2) and a Toss-style accent blue (#2F6BFF) within the phone interface. This is a screen-in-frame plus product-macro layout: describe the bike lock and QR sticker as the dominant left-and-center subject region, the entering smartphone with its scanner UI and the 'QR코드는 안장 밑에 있어요' / '문자 코드 입력하기' text occupying the right and overlapping center, and the lower-center grey subtitle pill reading '인식하면'. The overall feel is an authentic vertical Korean creator how-to macro insert: crisp tactile detail, natural medium-saturation grading, real daylight contrast, no film grain, no vignette, no lens distortion. Additional production context: this macro beat is the small wow moment of the tutorial, the instant the abstract on-screen flow connects to a physical object in the real world, so the hardware should look authentically used — scuffs, dust, fingerprints and faint scratches on the black housing, the sticker slightly weathered at its edges — rather than pristine product-shot clean. Keep the green release lever as the one pop of saturated colour against the otherwise neutral black-white-grey hardware so the eye is guided to the mechanism, and let the background pavement and wheel melt into soft macro blur so the QR sticker and the phone screen are the only two sharp planes in the frame. On the sticker, in a rough hand-stamped or hand-drawn blue ink with visible streaky brush-like texture and imperfect inking, is the wordmark reading exactly 'Curator T' in a bold condensed sans-serif. Directly beneath the wordmark, separated by a thin blue underline rule, is a small fine row of black Korean text reading exactly '토스를 발견하다'. The paper background shows a natural fibrous grain and faint speckle, evoking a handmade analog stamp print.
